questions.q: In a Maranao Torogan, what is the name of the intricately carved beam ends that feature 'okir' motifs and symbolize high social status?
questions.n: These are the most iconic decorative and structural elements of the Torogan, extending beyond the walls.

questions.q: Which structural element is unique to the Ifugao Fale and serves the functional purpose of preventing rodents from entering the rice storage area?
questions.n: These are the cylindrical wooden discs or 'rat guards' fitted onto the four main posts.

questions.q: The 'Bay Sinug' dwelling of the Tausug people is traditionally constructed using a layout of how many posts, representing the parts of the human body?
questions.n: The nine posts correspond to different parts of the human anatomy in Tausug cosmology.

questions.q: In the Ivatan Rakuh house, what is the primary reason for building the 'Kusina' as a separate structure from the main living area?
o: To provide more space for guests
To mitigate the risk of fire spreading
questions.n: Because the main house contains valuable items and heavy thatch, separate kitchens prevent cooking fires from destroying the whole home.

questions.q: Which part of the Bahay Kubo is specifically designed as a slatted wooden rack for drying kitchenware and storing water jars?
questions.n: This is the specialized slatted rack located near the window for air-drying dishes.

questions.q: The Kalinga 'Binayon' is most architecturally distinct from other Cordillera houses due to which feature?
o: Its lack of a roof ridge
questions.n: The Binayon is famous for its unique eight-sided geometry compared to the square Fale.

questions.q: Which term refers to the central post of a Tausug house, often considered the 'navel' of the structure?
questions.n: This central post is the spiritual and structural anchor of the Bay Sinug.

questions.q: In the Ifugao Fale, what is the name of the attic or loft area used specifically for storing harvested rice?
questions.n: The Pala is the elevated storage area located directly under the steep roof.

questions.q: What structural element in an Ivatan Rakuh helps secure the heavy layers of cogon thatch against high winds?
questions.n: This refers to the ridge of the roof which is heavily tied and reinforced to resist typhoon-force winds.

questions.q: Which part of the Bahay Kubo refers to the narrow gallery or passageway that often surrounds the central room?
questions.n: These are the outer areas or galleries that provide additional circulation and ventilation.

questions.q: In the Bahay Kubo, which part serves as the main multi-purpose space for both living and sleeping?
questions.n: This is the primary interior space used for receiving guests and family rest.

questions.q: The 'Halipan' in an Ifugao Fale is a cylindrical rat guard. On which part of the house is it installed?
questions.n: The guards are placed on the posts to block pests from climbing into the floor and attic.

questions.q: Which ethnic house is specifically known for its octagonal floor plan?
questions.n: The Kalinga Binayon is unique for its eight-sided geometry compared to the usual rectangular forms.

questions.q: What is the spiritual significance of the 'Tiyangi' in a Tausug Bay Sinug?
o: It represents the head of the family.
It symbolizes the connection to the sea.
It represents the 'navel' or center of the house body.
It is a guard against evil spirits from the earth.
questions.n: Tausug tradition views the house as a human body, with the central post as the navel.

questions.q: In the Ivatan Rakuh, what is the 'Sapa'?
o: The ridge tie of the roof.
questions.n: The Sapa provides the heavy thermal mass and storm resistance characteristic of Batanes.

questions.q: Which part of the Maranao Torogan serves as the royal bed or elevated sleeping area for the Datu?
questions.n: The Panggao is the ceremonial and private elevated bed reserved for the elite.

questions.q: In the Ifugao Fale, where is the 'Pala' located?
o: Attached to the main entrance ladder.
Along the perimeter of the walls.
questions.n: The Pala is the elevated tier used specifically for rice storage to keep it dry and smoke-cured.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the 'Banggerahan' in a Bahay Kubo?
o: To serve as a balcony for guests.
To store livestock during the night.
To provide a place for ritual offerings.
To dry kitchenware and store water jars.
questions.n: Its slatted design allows air to circulate around wet dishes and keeps water cool.

questions.q: The 'Tadjuk Pasung' are roof finials found on the Bay Sinug. What do they typically resemble?
questions.n: These carvings represent the Tausug's artistic connection to sea and sky myths.

questions.q: Which structural member of the Ifugao Fale acts as the floor joists to support the main planks?
questions.n: Fu-ig are the secondary beams that directly support the flooring boards.

questions.q: In the Torogan, which part is traditionally the very first post to be installed?
questions.n: The central post is the symbolic anchor and is the first to be erected during construction.

questions.q: The 'Vuvong' in an Ivatan house is critical because it:
o: Provides a base for the limestone walls.
Ties and secures the ridge of the heavy cogon roof.
Is the only window in the house.
Serves as the main drainage for rainwater.
questions.n: Without these heavy ties, the thick thatch could be lifted off by typhoon winds.

questions.q: Which area of the Bahay Kubo is an unroofed terrace used for bathing and laundry?
questions.n: The Batalan is positioned at the back to handle wet chores and keep the main house dry.

questions.q: In the Kalinga Binayon, what is the 'Dattagon'?
questions.n: In the octagonal plan, the Dattagon is the middle section where most activities occur.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the 'Silong' in lowland ethnic houses?
o: A sacred space for ancestral spirits.
Storage of agricultural tools and livestock.
A cooking area during the rainy season.
A guest room for visiting travelers.
questions.n: The elevated floor creates this space to keep items safe from floods and pests.

questions.q: In the Tausug Bay Sinug, the 'Sambi' is a term for:
questions.n: The Sambi is typically at the rear and may be slightly lower or detached.

questions.q: The 'Panolong' of the Torogan features the 'Pako Rabong' motif. What does 'Pako Rabong' specifically represent?
questions.n: This motif symbolizes life, growth, and fertility in Maranao art.

questions.q: In the Ifugao Fale, what structural purpose does the 'Huklub' serve?
o: It is the ladder used to enter the house.
It is the stone foundation at the base of the posts.
It is a perimeter beam that holds wallboards and acts as a shelf.
It is the main ridge beam of the roof.
questions.n: It ties the walls together at chest height and provides essential storage space.

questions.q: The 'Pahayahan' in a Rakuh house are intentionally small. Why?
o: To maintain structural integrity against heavy winds.
To keep the interior completely dark.
To hide from enemies or invaders.
Because they lack glass for larger windows.
questions.n: Large openings would weaken the limestone walls and allow pressure to build inside during a storm.

questions.q: Which specific element of the Bahay Kubo provides passive cooling by allowing hot air to escape?
questions.n: The steep angle and porous thatch allow heat to rise and exit through the top layers.

questions.q: In the Tausug Bay Sinug, what is the 'Pante'?
o: A porch or terrace at the front.
The central pillar of the house.
The rear exit to the kitchen.
questions.n: It serves as an entryway and a transition space from the outside to the interior.

questions.q: The 'Diongal' is an ornament found in the Torogan. Where exactly is it placed?
o: At the apex or ridge of the roof.
At the base of the central post.
questions.n: It is a pinnacle-like ornament that signifies the high status of the inhabitants.

questions.q: In the Ifugao Fale, what is the 'Gatid'?
questions.n: These are mortised into the beams and are slightly tilted outward to shed rain.

questions.q: The Kalinga Binayon uses 'Sipi' areas. What is their function?
o: Support posts for the roof ridge.
Holes in the floor for waste disposal.
Side platforms used for sleeping or storage.
questions.n: These surround the central Dattagon and provide specialized zones within the octagon.

questions.q: Which material is primarily used for the 'Kuvub' (roof) of an Ivatan Rakuh?
o: Bamboo slats covered in palm leaves.
Multiple layers of thick cogon thatch.
questions.n: It can be up to a meter thick to provide insulation and water resistance.

questions.q: What does the 'Dapogan' in a Bahay Kubo consist of?
o: A window for looking out at the farm.
A hearth with three stones for cooking.
A table for dining with guests.
questions.n: The stones support the cooking pot over an open fire.

questions.q: The 'Tukud' of a Torogan are unique because they are often made from:
questions.n: This preserves the strength of the wood and demonstrates the scale of the structure.

questions.q: In the Ifugao Fale, what is the 'Patuat'?
o: A central beam supporting the attic floor.
The rat guard on the post.
The floor joist for the living room.
questions.n: It spans the middle of the house to carry the load of the rice storage above.

questions.q: The 'Dagtong' in a Tausug house is used for:
o: Signaling the start of a ritual.
questions.n: These are usually long bamboo tubes kept near the entrance for washing feet.

questions.q: Which part of the Bahay Kubo is used for changing clothes or private storage?
questions.n: It is the only truly enclosed private space within the otherwise open plan.

questions.q: The 'Lantay' in a Rakuh house refers to:
questions.n: Even with stone walls, the interior living surface is made of wood for comfort.

questions.q: In the Kalinga Binayon, what is the 'Sokat'?
o: A skylight or ventilation opening in the roof.
The decorative post in the center.
questions.n: It allows smoke from the internal hearth to escape and admits light.

questions.q: Which of these houses is built using a 'three-tiered' vertical logic (Storage-Living-Underground)?
questions.n: It clearly separates the attic (Pala), living floor, and the open silong area.

questions.q: In the Maranao Torogan, what is the function of the 'Barimbingan'?
o: They are the thick, often carved wooden wall planks.
They are the stairs for commoners.
They are the water jars kept in the kitchen.
questions.n: These provide the enclosure and are often adorned with beautiful okir patterns.

questions.q: What is the 'Lawang' in a Tausug house?
questions.n: It is the threshold into the main Luma (house body).

questions.q: The 'Panpet' in an Ivatan house is a:
o: Large roof beam that supports the heavy thatch layers.
questions.n: It provides the internal framework for the massive cogon roof.

questions.q: In the Bahay Kubo, what are the 'Gigilid' used for?
o: Circulation and passage around the main room.
questions.n: These galleries allow movement without disturbing those in the center of the Bulwagan.

questions.q: The Kalinga Binayon's 'Paratag' is used for:
o: A storage shelf for various household items.
questions.n: It helps organize the interior by keeping items off the floor.

questions.q: In an Ifugao Fale, what are the 'Bagat'?
o: The wooden planks used for the floor.
The four main outer posts of the house.
The central beam for the attic.
The heavy layers of roof thatch.
questions.n: These carry the entire weight of the house and are the points where Halipan are placed.

questions.q: Which house uses 'limestone and coral walls' to resist extreme weather?
questions.n: This is a unique adaptation to the harsh typhoon climate of Batanes.

questions.q: The 'Luma' in a Tausug Bay Sinug refers to:
o: The decorative bird motif on the roof.
The main body or shell of the house.
The ladder used to reach the porch.
The kitchen detached from the house.
questions.n: It is the primary structural unit elevated on the nine-post foundation.

questions.q: Which part of the Torogan is characterized by whole tree trunks as pillars?
questions.n: These massive supports are necessary for the heavy weight of the royal structure.

questions.q: In the Bahay Kubo, why is the floor traditionally slatted with bamboo?
o: To allow occupants to see intruders below.
To make the house easier to clean by sweeping dust down.
To reduce the cost of building materials.
To allow air to flow up and cool the interior.
questions.n: The slats facilitate passive ventilation, which is vital in the humid lowlands.

questions.q: The Kalinga Binayon's 'Chokar' are:
o: The heavy floor beams supporting the structure.
The thatch used for the roof.
questions.n: These bridge the posts and carry the load of the Dattagon and Sipi.

questions.q: In an Ifugao Fale, what is the 'Ga-ob'?
o: The rat guard on the post.
The thick, low-extending cogon thatch roof.
questions.n: It protects the wooden structure from the heavy rains of the Cordilleras.

questions.q: The 'Hagdan' in a Tausug house is the:
o: Ladder or stairs to the porch.
questions.n: Since the house is on stilts, this is the only way to enter.

questions.q: Which Ivatan house part is a 'separate structure for cooking to prevent fire'?
questions.n: Its separation is a classic safety feature in indigenous housing with thatched roofs.

questions.q: The 'Piyong' in a Binayon are:
o: The wooden wallboards of the house.
The support posts at the corners.
The floor beams under the Dattagon.
questions.n: These form the octagonal enclosure of the Kalinga dwelling.

questions.q: Which of these features is a decorative roof finial in a Tausug Bay Sinug?
questions.n: These ornate carvings represent bird or dragon motifs on the roof ridge.

questions.q: In a Bahay Kubo, where would you find the 'Silid'?
o: Attached to the Batalan for laundry.
Under the house with the animals.
questions.n: It is usually a small partitioned space for sleeping or changing within the main floor plan.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the 'Binayon' house of the Kalinga people in terms of its unique interior floor levels?
o: It features a central floor area called 'dattagon' lower than the side 'sipi' areas.
The floor is inclined toward the center to collect rainwater.
It has a uniform, single-level floor made entirely of stone.
The central floor is elevated higher than the sleeping platforms.
questions.n: The sunken central area creates a clear functional distinction within the octagonal plan.

questions.q: In the construction of the Ivatan Rakuh, why is the 'lime mortar' specifically used for the limestone walls?
o: To provide flexibility during earthquakes and high wind pressure.
To make the house lightweight for easy relocation.
To attract heat during the cold northern winters.
To act as a waterproof paint to prevent moss growth.
questions.n: Lime mortar is less brittle than modern cement, allowing the stone walls to 'breathe' and shift slightly without collapsing.

questions.q: The 'Panolong' is a distinct feature of the Maranao Torogan. What structural member does it actually serve as an extension of?
questions.n: The panolong are the protruding ends of the floor beams that support the entire structure.

questions.q: In a Tausug 'Bay Sinug', the post representing the human 'shoulders' is placed in which part of the 9-post grid?
o: The posts flanking the central 'navel' post.
questions.n: The grid maps the human torso, placing shoulder posts at the upper corners relative to the navel.

questions.q: Which specific part of the Bahay Kubo provides a storage area for 'palay' (unhusked rice) inside the main house?
questions.n: While used for privacy, the silid often doubles as a secure storage area for family valuables and grain.

questions.q: The 'Fale' is built without nails. What indigenous joinery method is primarily used to secure the 'Gatid' (wallboards)?
questions.n: Wallboards are fitted into grooves in the beams, allowing for expansion and easy disassembly.

questions.q: In the Maranao Torogan, what is the 'Diongal'?
o: A secret passage under the floorboards.
An ornate pinnacle or ridge decoration on the roof.
questions.n: This serves as a crowning ornament that emphasizes the height and importance of the royal house.

questions.q: Which feature of the Ivatan 'Rakuh' house helps prevent the heavy cogon roof from being blown away by 'uplift' forces during a typhoon?
o: Opening all the windows to let wind pass through.
A net of heavy ropes or 'vuvong' tied over the thatch.
Making the roof flat to reduce wind resistance.
Using stones as shingles instead of grass.
questions.n: The net is anchored to the stone walls or heavy beams to keep the thatch compressed.

questions.q: In the Kalinga 'Binayon', what is the purpose of the 'Sokat'?
o: Ventilation and light as it is a removable roof panel.
A drain for the kitchen area.
A ritual entrance for priests only.
questions.n: This allows the occupants to control the climate and clear smoke from the cooking fire.

questions.q: Why are the four main posts of an Ifugao Fale (Bagat) buried in the ground instead of sitting on stones like the Maranao Torogan?
o: It was a religious requirement of the Ifugao.
Because stone was unavailable in the Cordilleras.
To resist the lateral forces of mountain slope landslides and earthquakes.
To keep the wood moist so it doesn't crack.
questions.n: Deeply embedded posts provide better anchorage in the soft, sloping soil of the terraces.

questions.q: In the 'Bay Sinug', the Tausug kitchen is called the 'Sambi'. Why is it often detached or built on a lower level?
o: Because only slaves were allowed to enter the kitchen.
To follow a specific Islamic law regarding food prep.
It was designed to float away in case of a flood.
To prevent cooking smoke and heat from entering the main 'Luma'.
questions.n: Separating the kitchen improves the comfort of the living and sleeping quarters.

questions.q: The 'Panpet' in an Ivatan Rakuh refers to the horizontal roof beams. What is their primary load-bearing role?
o: Serving as the main floor structure.
Supporting the weight of the thick, heavy cogon thatch.
Connecting the main house to the separate kitchen.
questions.n: Because the thatch can be several feet thick, the internal timber frame must be exceptionally strong.

questions.q: What is the function of the 'Gigilid' in the Bahay Kubo beyond circulation?
o: It is where the family keeps their most sacred ancestral shrines.
It is the area specifically used for animal pens.
It acts as a buffer zone that prevents direct sunlight from heating the 'Bulwagan'.
It serves as the main structural support for the roof.
questions.n: The outer gallery shades the inner living area, keeping it significantly cooler.

questions.q: Which of these describe the 'Pako Rabong' motif found in Maranao architecture?
o: Abstract representations of the sea waves.
Stylized fern fronds symbolizing life and growth.
Geometric shapes representing the stars and moon.
questions.n: It is a central motif in 'Okir' art, representing organic vitality.

questions.q: In an Ifugao Fale, the 'Pala' (attic) is used for rice storage. How is the rice protected from moisture and insects there?
o: Heat and smoke from the hearth below dry and preserve the grain.
The rice is stored in airtight clay jars.
The attic is lined with metal sheets.
The roof is made of waterproof plastic.
questions.n: The open-fire cooking in the bulwagan naturally cures the rice stored in the loft above.

questions.q: The 'Dagtong' in a Tausug house are bamboo water tubes. Where are they traditionally placed?
o: In the center of the 'Bulwagan' for drinking.
At the foot of the 'Hagdan' (stairs) for washing feet before entering.
On the roof to collect rainwater.
questions.n: This maintains the cleanliness of the elevated living space.

questions.q: What structural role do the 'Tukud' (columns) of a Torogan play in relation to earthquakes?
o: They are bolted deep into the bedrock for rigidity.
They sit on large stones to allow the house to 'sway' safely during tremors.
They are made of flexible bamboo to absorb shocks.
They are designed to collapse easily to save the roof.
questions.n: The lack of rigid anchorage prevents the timber frame from snapping under seismic stress.

questions.q: In the Kalinga Binayon, the 'Paratag' is a shelf. Where is it specifically located?
o: Along the interior walls above the 'Sipi' platforms.
Hanging from the center of the roof.
questions.n: It utilizes the wall space for storage, keeping the floor area clear.

questions.q: Why does the 'Batalan' in a Bahay Kubo have a slatted floor made of bamboo poles?
o: To reduce the weight of the house.
To serve as a cage for chickens.
To make it more comfortable for sleeping.
To allow water to drain directly to the ground during washing.
questions.n: The open slats prevent water from pooling and rotting the structure.

questions.q: In the Ivatan Rakuh, the 'Kusina' (kitchen) is often built with 'lighter' materials compared to the main house. Why?
o: Because the kitchen is less important than the living room.
Because limestone was only reserved for the elite.
To allow cooking smoke to escape through the walls.
So it can be easily rebuilt if a cooking fire destroys it.
questions.n: Separation and lighter construction isolate the fire risk from the main stone living quarters.
